title: Lightly Spiced French Duck Confit
description: A classic Alsatian dish featuring tender duck leg confit, lightly spiced with garam masala and paired with a floral emulsified sauce, perfect for a solo dinner.
instructions: Cure the duck legs with kosher salt, black pepper, and garam masala for at least 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Preheat the oven to 275 degrees Fahrenheit.
Rinse the cured duck legs and pat them dry with paper towels.
Heat the olive oil and duck fat in a large Dutch oven over medium heat.
Seal the duck legs until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes per side.
Add the garlic, white wine, thyme, and rosemary to the pot.
Cover the pot and transfer it to the preheated oven.
Cook the duck confit for 2 1/2 hours, or until the meat is tender and easily shreds with a fork.
Let the confit cool in the pot for 30 minutes before refrigerating it overnight.
Emulsify the cooking liquid with a little water to create a light sauce.
Serve the confit with the emulsified sauce spooned over the top.
